_doc: The metronome's phase table (OPS_METRONOME_PROVE_IN_SHADOW, OPS_METRONOME_MIGRATE_CLOCKS_FENCED; design/RimMandrake/operations_metronome_strategy_2026-11-02.md §2, §8 step 5). Read by src/RimMandrake/Utils/metronome.py, validated by `metronome.py lint`. Phases run in the order sense, remember, raise, ring, dispatch, chores; a phase is due when beat % every == offset, when it is overdue, or when one of its wall-clock slots is due. budget_s bounds the whole beat; raise and ring (and any overdue phase) are reserved first. A phase without owns is in shadow: its command only reads or writes inside {state} (ops_watch's own store there, the Dispatcher's dry tick). A phase with owns has replaced those old timers (disabled at cutover, one clock a day) and runs its real command carrying {gen}, its ownership generation (metronome.may_act). raise owns rm-restart-reconcile.timer since 2026-11-04: 500 of 500 shadow passes exited 0, max 1.2 s; the real pass reads transcripts and may file in process, so 12 s. limit_s values are ESTIMATES (ops_watch: 73 s for all 20 families, so 2 per beat); measure them from beats.jsonl before cutover (step 6); first shadow beats, 2026-11-04: steve+testing 1.5 s, but accounts+codex and disk+timers each overran 15 s, so per-family timing decides the pairing before cutover. chores has no shadow command yet: its four timers stay the owners. sense runs ops_watch --compose since 2026-11-05 (every family not measured this beat carried from its series with observed_at, alarms and the health verdict made on the beat that measures flow, which joins testing for its ctx, so testing sits between flow and the light production), fenced by {gen}; its codex and queues reads are cached (24 s and 16 s alone before, ~4 s and ~3 s warm).

chores.why_no_command: scratch pressure, account plan and usage keep their own timers until cutover
